title: Hoisting and TDZ Check
description: Predict what var, let, and const do when read before their declaration line.

questions.explanation: `var x` is hoisted and auto-initialized to `undefined` before the assignment line runs.
`let` is hoisted but stays in the Temporal Dead Zone until its declaration runs — reading it early throws a `ReferenceError`.
`const` follows the same TDZ rule as `let` — hoisted but uninitialized until the declaration line.

questions.prompt: After execution passes a `let` declaration's line, how does the binding behave?

options.text: Behaves like a normal, initialized variable

questions.explanation: The TDZ ends exactly at the declaration line — after that, `let`/`const` behave like any other variable.

questions.prompt: Where does the Temporal Dead Zone end for a given `let`/`const` binding?

options.text: At the end of the enclosing block
At the end of the file

questions.explanation: The TDZ starts at the top of the scope and ends exactly when the declaration line executes — not at the block's closing brace.

questions.prompt: Which statement about hoisting is true?

options.text: Only `var` is hoisted; `let`/`const` are not hoisted at all
`var`, `let`, and `const` are all hoisted, but only `var` is auto-initialized to `undefined`
Hoisting only applies inside functions, never at module scope

questions.explanation: All three are hoisted (the engine reserves the binding), but `var` is immediately set to `undefined` while `let`/`const` stay uninitialized (TDZ) until their line runs.
